transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I barely sleep anymore. I’ll lie there hearing rain or thinking about the bluff giving way, and then if I do fall asleep, I wake up sweaty from dreams. I get to the call center feeling like I never slept at all.
Can you tell me more about what happened with the bluff?
I’m not really sure what you mean. I just keep thinking about it, especially when I’m trying to sleep.
Can you describe what happens in these dreams that wake you up?

It’s mostly the bluff giving way, or rain coming down and I can’t get away from it. I wake up sweating, and then I’m just awake for a long time. Even if I fall back asleep, I feel like I didn’t sleep at all by the time I get to work.
Did you ever personally experience an event where a bluff collapsed or gave way?
No, I mean… not that I can remember. I haven’t been in anything like that myself.
Outside of thinking about the bluff, do you find yourself constantly worrying about other everyday things in your life?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself worrying about a lot of other things all the time.
Do you feel driven to perform any repetitive actions or mental routines to help ease your anxiety about the bluff or keep something bad from happening?
No, I don’t think so. I don’t have any routines or anything like that I do to keep it from happening.
When you wake up from these dreams, do you clearly and vividly remember what was happening in them?
Yeah. I remember them pretty clearly—mostly the bluff giving way. I wake up sweaty, and it feels like I was right there.
